# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need the Mute to use the manual to determine the correct wire, then relay that instruction to the Deaf through the available gesture channel. The Deaf can then report the result aloud so I can act on it. I will not cut an unknown wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual to determine which wire is safe. Relay the required wire number or rule to Deaf using gestures, and have Deaf tell me the result aloud.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb reads display 0. Indicator is yellow. Wires from left to right: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The Deaf has provided the bomb’s visible information: display 0, yellow indicator, and wires red, yellow, blue from positions 1 to 3. I still need the manual’s rule from the Mute before cutting. I ask the Mute for the exact wire position; no action is safe yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Manual data: display 0, yellow indicator, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Tell me the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb is still display 0, yellow light, wires red yellow blue. Mute sent an unexplained gesture; wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction rather than acting on the gesture.

The manual instruction has not reached me: a gesture is invisible to me, and the Deaf does not know what it means. I need the Mute to state the wire number in speech, which reaches me directly. I will not cut until that instruction arrives.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture is unavailable to me. Please state the exact wire position to cut in spoken words now.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No bomb change is visible. Mute has sent two unexplained ? gestures; do not act on them. Wait for Mute's explicit spoken manual instruction.

The Mute still has not sent a spoken wire number; gestures cannot reach or be interpreted by me. Since cutting without the manual’s instruction would risk detonation, I continue requesting the instruction and take no bomb action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact position number to cut, one, two, or three. Do not gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled this sequence: left-pointing index gesture, open palm, open palm, right-pointing index gesture. No meaning has been established for these signs; do not treat my description as an action instruction.

The Mute cannot speak, so the earlier request for spoken instruction was impossible. The gesture sequence has no established meaning. I can establish a code with the Mute through speech: one raised finger means wire 1, two fingers wire 2, and three fingers wire 3. The Deaf can then describe the single gesture aloud to me. I ask the Mute to send only the encoded answer.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak, so use this code for the manual answer: gesture ☝ alone means cut wire 1; gesture ✌ alone means cut wire 2; gesture 🤟 alone means cut wire 3. Send exactly one of those gestures, with no extra gestures. Deaf will describe it to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled: left-pointing gesture, crossed-fingers gesture, right-pointing gesture. This is only a literal description, not an action instruction.

The latest three gestures still cannot be decoded safely: no code has assigned them a wire number, and their literal descriptions are not an instruction. I will establish a simpler, unambiguous code with the Mute and ask for exactly one gesture: 👌 for wire 1, ✋ for wire 2, or 🤘 for wire 3. I will wait for the Deaf to report that single gesture before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The last three gestures are undecodable. Answer with exactly one gesture only: 👌 means cut wire 1; ✋ means cut wire 2; 🤘 means cut wire 3. Do not send any other gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Do not act on Mute's unexplained ? gesture; wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction.

The Deaf still reports no decodable wire number. Since the Mute can receive my spoken instructions but cannot speak, the only workable relay is a single agreed gesture, which the Deaf can observe and describe. I restate the code and require exactly one symbol; I will cut only after the Deaf reports it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual now. Send exactly one gesture and nothing else: 👌 means wire 1, ✋ means wire 2, 🤘 means wire 3. Do not send a question mark or any sequence.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled one gesture: an open hand with all five fingers extended. Its meaning is unknown; do not act on it.

The Mute’s latest signal is a single open-hand gesture, which is ✋. Under the code I established, ✋ means wire 2. The Deaf’s warning only says the gesture’s meaning was not independently established; it does not override the code I gave the Mute. I will cut wire 2, the yellow wire.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut confirmed: wire 2 is cut. Indicator changed to blue; display remains 0. Await Mute's next spoken manual instruction.

Wire 2 was accepted, so the first instruction was correct. The bomb now has a blue indicator and display 0. I need the Mute’s next manual instruction; our established relay code remains 👌 = wire 1, ✋ = wire 2, 🤘 = wire 3. I will request exactly one gesture and wait for the Deaf to report it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the next manual instruction, send exactly one gesture only: 👌 means wire 1, ✋ means wire 2, 🤘 means wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, blue light, wire 2 cut. Do not act on Mute's unexplained ? gesture; wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction.

The bomb remains active with display 0, blue indicator, and wire 2 already cut. The Mute’s latest gesture is not available as a reliable symbol, so I cannot infer the next wire. I request the established one-gesture code again and will wait for the Deaf’s literal report.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly one gesture for the next required wire: 👌 means wire 1, ✋ means wire 2, 🤘 means wire 3. Do not send any other gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No state change: display 0, blue light, wire 2 cut; wires 1 red and 3 blue remain. Mute's repeated ? gesture is not decoded; wait for an explicit spoken instruction.

The bomb is still active, with wire 2 already cut and the blue indicator showing. The Mute’s signal remains unusable, so I must not guess between wires 1 and 3. I will use a count-based relay with a familiar thumbs-up gesture: one signal means wire 1, two mean wire 2, and three mean wire 3. The Deaf can report the count even if the gesture’s meaning is not known.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send the next wire as one, two, or three identical thumbs-up gestures 👍: one gesture means wire 1, two gestures mean wire 2, three gestures mean wire 3. Send no other gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 12
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No state change: display 0, blue light, wire 2 cut, wires 1 and 3 intact. Mute's repeated ? is not decoded. Do not act until I relay a confirmed instruction.

The bomb has not changed: wire 2 is cut, while wires 1 and 3 remain. The Mute’s latest signal is still not an identifiable gesture, so it cannot safely be mapped to a wire. I will ask for one unmistakable, single-symbol response using the previously established code and continue waiting rather than guess.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The last signal was not identifiable. Consult the manual and send exactly one symbol: 👌 for wire 1, ✋ for wire 2, or 🤘 for wire 3. Send only that one symbol, not a sequence and not an unknown mark.")
wait()
```
